concepts.title: Buy-side liquidity
concepts.definition: Buy stops may sit above a visible high.
concepts.rule: Mark a completed high and the price immediately above it.
concepts.example: A prior high at 20020 remains visible above price.
concepts.lookalike: A low below the market is labeled buy-side.
concepts.objective: Mark a meaningful high and explain why buy stops may sit above it.

concepts.title: Sell-side liquidity
concepts.definition: Sell stops may sit below a visible low.
concepts.rule: Mark the low before looking for a run through it.
concepts.example: Price approaches yesterday’s low from above.
concepts.lookalike: A high is labeled sell-side.
concepts.objective: Mark a meaningful low and explain why sell stops may sit below it.

concepts.title: Equal highs and equal lows
concepts.definition: Two or more swing extremes cluster at similar prices.
concepts.rule: Declare a tolerance in ticks and compare confirmed pivots.
concepts.example: Two highs one tick apart meet a two-tick tolerance.
concepts.lookalike: Highs six ticks apart exceed that tolerance.
concepts.objective: Identify relatively equal extremes. Record the tick tolerance used in the exercise.

concepts.title: Liquidity sweep
concepts.definition: Price trades through a previously identified liquidity level.
concepts.rule: Record the level, breach and subsequent response separately.
concepts.example: A high at 20010 trades to 20011 before price closes below.
concepts.lookalike: Price approaches 20010 but peaks at 20009.75.
concepts.objective: Mark which level traded through and what price did afterward. Use separate labels for the sweep and any later reversal confirmation.

concepts.title: Draw on liquidity
concepts.definition: A liquidity level serves as a conditional price objective.
concepts.rule: Record the objective and invalidation before advancing replay.
concepts.example: A prior high is selected before the next bar opens.
concepts.lookalike: The target is selected after seeing the outcome.
concepts.objective: Select a plausible price objective before revealing the next candles.

concepts.title: Swing highs and lows
concepts.definition: A local pivot is a high or low relative to neighboring candles.
concepts.rule: For a three-bar exercise wait for the right-hand bar to close.
concepts.example: The middle high exceeds both adjacent highs.
concepts.lookalike: A forming right-hand bar is counted as complete.
concepts.objective: Label a pivot and identify when enough candles have closed to recognize it.

concepts.title: Swing hierarchy
concepts.definition: Swings can be nested into short-, intermediate- and long-term structures.
concepts.rule: Compare neighboring pivots of the same rank before promoting a swing.
concepts.example: An intermediate high sits between two lower short-term highs.
concepts.lookalike: A lone pivot is labeled long-term without surrounding structure.
concepts.aliases: STH ITH LTH STL ITL LTL
concepts.objective: Mark nested swings and explain which one matters for the current idea. Use an original lab diagram for the three levels.

concepts.title: Market structure shift
concepts.definition: Directional delivery changes through a relevant swing.
concepts.rule: Choose the swing in advance and assess displacement through it.
concepts.example: After a low sweep price displaces above a marked lower high.
concepts.lookalike: A wick touches the high without the required break.
concepts.objective: Identify the reference swing, the break, and the quality of the move through it.

concepts.title: Displacement
concepts.definition: A decisive directional move reprices through an area.
concepts.rule: Compare range, closes and overlap with the preceding candles.
concepts.example: Expanding bodies close away from a congested range.
concepts.lookalike: Several overlapping small bars remain inside it.
concepts.objective: Identify decisive directional movement and check whether it creates an imbalance.

concepts.title: Continuation versus reversal
concepts.definition: A continuation resumes prior delivery while a reversal changes its direction.
concepts.rule: Identify the structural level whose failure would change the thesis.
concepts.example: A retracement holds the selected low then makes a new high.
concepts.lookalike: One opposing candle is called a reversal without structural change.
concepts.objective: Compare two charts that begin with a pullback but resolve in different directions.

concepts.title: Dealing range selection
concepts.definition: A selected swing high and low frame the price interval under study.
concepts.rule: Record both anchors and timeframe.
concepts.example: A 20000–20100 impulse defines the exercise range.
concepts.lookalike: One anchor is moved after the entry to improve the result.
concepts.objective: Choose the two anchors and record the timeframe.

sources.label: TTrades — Choosing Dealing and Displacement Ranges

concepts.title: Equilibrium
concepts.definition: The midpoint divides a chosen range into equal halves.
concepts.rule: Average the two range anchors.
concepts.example: The midpoint of 20000–20100 is 20050.
concepts.lookalike: 20060 is labeled the midpoint of that range.
concepts.objective: Calculate the midpoint of the selected range.

concepts.title: Premium and discount
concepts.definition: Premium is above equilibrium and discount is below it within the chosen range.
concepts.rule: Compare current price to the same range midpoint.
concepts.example: 20075 is premium inside 20000–20100.
concepts.lookalike: A midpoint calculated on a different range is used.
concepts.objective: Place the current price in the upper or lower half of the chosen range.

concepts.title: Internal and external range liquidity
concepts.definition: Internal references lie inside the range and external objectives beyond its boundaries.
concepts.rule: Mark the boundaries first, then classify references.
concepts.example: An internal gap and a prior high beyond the range are labeled separately.
concepts.lookalike: An internal gap is labeled an external extreme.
concepts.objective: Distinguish a reference inside the range from liquidity beyond its extreme.

concepts.title: Optimal Trade Entry
concepts.definition: OTE frames a deeper retracement of a selected swing.
concepts.rule: Anchor the measurement consistently and require the parent setup.
concepts.example: The retracement area is defined before price returns.
concepts.lookalike: Fib anchors are shifted until they fit the eventual low.
concepts.objective: Select the impulse leg, plot the retracement, and explain why that swing was chosen.

concepts.title: Fair value gap
concepts.definition: A three-candle sequence leaves a non-overlapping interval between the outer candles.
concepts.rule: For a bullish gap compare candle one high with candle three low.
concepts.example: First high 20000 and third low 20002 leave two points.
concepts.lookalike: Third low 19999 overlaps the first candle.
concepts.objective: Mark the three-candle formation and the boundaries of the non-overlapping area.

concepts.title: Inversion fair value gap
concepts.definition: A breached FVG can become an opposite-side reference.
concepts.rule: Mark the gap and apply the selected close-through rule before assessing a retest.
concepts.example: A bullish gap is closed through then retested from below.
concepts.lookalike: A wick enters the gap while the close-through condition remains unmet.
concepts.objective: Mark the original FVG, the qualifying breach, and the subsequent interaction from the opposite side.

concepts.title: Balanced price range
concepts.definition: Opposing imbalances overlap across a common price interval.
concepts.rule: Draw each gap independently and shade only their intersection.
concepts.lookalike: Two disjoint gaps are combined into one zone.
concepts.objective: Mark the overlap between opposing imbalances and identify its boundaries.

concepts.title: Volume imbalance
concepts.definition: An interval between adjacent candle bodies can exist even when their wicks overlap.
concepts.rule: Compare bodies of adjacent candles and mark the intervening prices.
concepts.example: A body ends at 20000 and the next begins at 20002.
concepts.lookalike: Two overlapping bodies are treated as a body gap.
concepts.objective: Identify the adjacent candle-body interval and compare it with a three-candle FVG.

concepts.title: Consequent encroachment
concepts.definition: CE is the midpoint of the selected inefficiency.
concepts.rule: Average that zone’s upper and lower price boundaries.
concepts.example: A gap from 20000 to 20004 has CE at 20002.
concepts.lookalike: The full session midpoint is used instead.
concepts.objective: Mark the midpoint of the specific imbalance and state which boundaries produced it.

sources.label: TTrades — FVG lesson with CE coverage

concepts.title: Order block
concepts.definition: An eligible candle or candle sequence anchors an area preceding displacement.
concepts.rule: Identify the departure and its structural context before drawing the zone.
concepts.example: An opposing candle precedes expansion through the chosen swing.
concepts.lookalike: Every opposing candle in a range is labeled an order block.
concepts.objective: Identify the candle or zone, the confirming move, and the relevant boundary.

concepts.title: Breaker block
concepts.definition: A failed block may become a reference from the opposite direction.
concepts.rule: Identify the original block, its failure and subsequent retest.
concepts.example: A qualifying bullish block fails then is approached from below.
concepts.lookalike: An intact block is labeled a breaker.
concepts.objective: Mark the structure sequence, block failure, and potential opposite-side retest.

concepts.title: Mitigation block
concepts.definition: A block associated with a failed swing can become relevant on return.
concepts.rule: Locate the failed swing, structural break and return to its origin.
concepts.example: A failed push precedes a break and revisit to its associated area.
concepts.lookalike: An arbitrary retest has no preceding failure sequence.
concepts.objective: Identify the sequence that qualifies the area and the return being studied.

concepts.title: Rejection block
concepts.definition: A rejection wick defines a price interval at a relevant extreme.
concepts.rule: Mark the wick-to-body interval and contextual high or low.
concepts.example: A long upper wick at a marked high forms the candidate zone.
concepts.lookalike: The entire unrelated candle body is selected.
concepts.objective: Use the original lesson to mark the wick-based area and explain its context.

concepts.title: PD array selection
concepts.definition: Premium and discount arrays provide candidate areas in the current narrative.
concepts.rule: Rank eligible areas by location, direction and the chosen model.
concepts.example: A selected discount array aligns with a bullish scenario.
concepts.lookalike: Every visible gap is equally eligible regardless of direction.
concepts.objective: Choose among candidate areas using bias, location, timeframe, and the chosen playbook.

concepts.title: Asia session range
concepts.definition: The high and low within the stated Asia window define its range.
concepts.rule: Fix the session clock and include only bars inside the window.
concepts.example: The highest in-window bar sets the range high.
concepts.lookalike: A London bar expands the prior Asia range.
concepts.objective: Mark the session boundaries, range high, and range low.

concepts.title: London kill zone
concepts.definition: A London-session study window limits time-based forex observations.
concepts.rule: Convert the dated source window to the chart timezone.
concepts.example: A setup forms inside the recorded window.
concepts.lookalike: A UTC offset is reused across a DST change.
concepts.objective: Mark the named window and how price interacts with the earlier range.

concepts.title: New York AM kill zone
concepts.definition: A defined morning window frames New York setup study.
concepts.rule: Record the source, instrument and exact eligible window.
concepts.example: A timestamp belongs to the chosen AM window.
concepts.lookalike: A PM setup is counted in AM statistics.
concepts.objective: Identify which AM window the selected lesson and market use.

concepts.title: New York lunch and PM
concepts.definition: Midday and afternoon periods give different contexts for studying delivery.
concepts.rule: Record the actual New York time and session phase.
concepts.example: An afternoon return is tagged PM.
concepts.lookalike: An afternoon signal is credited to the morning window.
concepts.objective: Compare midday behavior with the afternoon opportunity window.

concepts.title: New York midnight open
concepts.definition: The New York midnight reference uses the opening price of that local timestamp.
concepts.rule: Locate 00:00 in America/New_York for the chosen date.
concepts.example: The midnight bar opens at 20010 and its open is retained.
concepts.lookalike: The exchange trading-day open is substituted.
concepts.objective: Plot the price at midnight in New York and label its date and timezone.

concepts.title: Previous day high and low
concepts.definition: The completed prior trading day supplies two reference extremes.
concepts.rule: Fix the trading-session definition and mark its completed high and low.
concepts.example: Yesterday’s levels are frozen for today’s exercise.
concepts.lookalike: Today’s unfinished extremes replace yesterday’s.
concepts.objective: Mark the completed prior day using the selected session definition.

concepts.title: Previous week high and low
concepts.definition: The prior completed week provides weekly liquidity references.
concepts.rule: Use the prior full trading week on the selected contract.
concepts.example: Last week’s extremes stay fixed as this week develops.
concepts.lookalike: The current partial week is used.
concepts.objective: Mark the prior completed week and check whether either extreme has since traded.

concepts.title: Previous month high and low
concepts.definition: The prior completed trading month supplies monthly reference extremes.
concepts.rule: Mark the last full month before drilling down to intraday charts.
concepts.example: October extremes are used for a November exercise.
concepts.lookalike: The current month’s evolving high is called previous month high.
concepts.objective: Mark the prior completed month before zooming into the intraday chart.

concepts.title: Daily, weekly and monthly opens
concepts.definition: Each period starts at its first eligible traded opening price under a stated session convention.
concepts.rule: Record each period and the opening bar separately.
concepts.example: Daily example: Tuesday’s first eligible bar opens at 20020. Weekly example: the week’s first eligible bar opens at 20005. Monthly example: the month’s first eligible bar opens at 19980.
concepts.lookalike: Calendar midnight is silently substituted for all three opens.
concepts.objective: Display the first eligible price for each period under the lab’s stated session convention. Include one labeled example per timeframe.

concepts.title: New day and new week opening gaps
concepts.definition: A daily or weekly reopening can leave an interval from the prior closing reference.
concepts.rule: Capture both boundary prices under the source’s trading-day definition.
concepts.example: Previous close 20010 and reopen 20014 define a four-point interval.
concepts.lookalike: An ordinary intraday FVG is labeled an opening gap.
concepts.objective: Mark each gap’s two boundary prices and label the period. Give each half of this card its own video button.

concepts.title: Higher-timeframe narrative
concepts.definition: A conditional scenario links larger-timeframe references with current delivery.
concepts.rule: Write the objective and the price action that would weaken the idea.
concepts.example: The scenario is recorded before the lower-timeframe setup.
concepts.lookalike: The narrative is constructed after the exit.
concepts.objective: Write the objective, supporting evidence, and condition that would change the idea.

concepts.title: Daily directional bias
concepts.definition: Daily bias is a working hypothesis about directional delivery.
concepts.rule: Identify supporting references and a condition that cancels the idea.
concepts.example: A bullish bias has a documented objective and invalidation.
concepts.lookalike: A preferred direction is retained after its premise fails.
concepts.objective: Build a working view and revise it when its evidence fails.

concepts.title: Power of Three
concepts.definition: Accumulation, manipulation and distribution describe a proposed sequence.
concepts.rule: Show the range, move through one side and eventual directional leg.
concepts.example: An early range gives way to a low run and bullish expansion.
concepts.lookalike: Three arbitrary candles are assigned one phase each.
concepts.objective: Identify accumulation, manipulation, and distribution on the same sequence.

concepts.title: Daily profiles
concepts.definition: A profile describes how delivery unfolds through successive sessions.
concepts.rule: Compare the evolving session with the profile prerequisites.
concepts.example: A candidate profile remains conditional until its features develop.
concepts.lookalike: The completed day is used to claim an earlier confirmed signal.
concepts.objective: Track how the day develops across sessions and state which profile remains plausible.

concepts.title: No-trade conditions
concepts.definition: A written filter rules out a session or entry.
concepts.rule: Decide which missing evidence or event excludes participation.
concepts.example: No eligible trigger appears before the window closes.
concepts.lookalike: An expired entry is accepted to avoid a skipped day.
concepts.objective: Define what would make the learner skip a session or reject an entry.

concepts.title: Bullish SMT
concepts.definition: Corresponding lows diverge when only one related market breaks its reference low.
concepts.rule: Align timestamps and compare the same market event.
concepts.example: NQ makes a lower low while ES holds its corresponding low.
concepts.lookalike: Lows from unrelated sessions are compared.
concepts.objective: Compare corresponding lows. Identify when one market makes a lower low while the paired market holds its prior low.

concepts.title: Bearish SMT
concepts.definition: Corresponding highs diverge when only one market breaks its reference high.
concepts.rule: Synchronize both instruments before choosing reference highs.
concepts.example: ES makes a higher high and NQ holds below its matched high.
concepts.lookalike: Both instruments make matching higher highs.
concepts.objective: Compare corresponding highs. Identify when only one market exceeds its prior high.

concepts.title: Matching NQ and ES swings
concepts.definition: A valid comparison uses corresponding pivots from the same event.
concepts.rule: Use comparable contracts, timeframe and aligned session timestamps.
concepts.example: Both chosen reference highs formed in the same opening move.
concepts.lookalike: A prior-day ES pivot is paired with a later unrelated NQ peak.
concepts.objective: Synchronize both charts and require the learner to justify the chosen pair of swings.

concepts.title: Higher-to-lower-timeframe alignment
concepts.definition: A larger objective frames a smaller setup area and execution trigger.
concepts.rule: Record all three timeframes and the role of each.
concepts.example: Daily objective, hourly area and minute trigger are documented.
concepts.lookalike: A minute entry is justified by an unrelated weekly pattern.
concepts.objective: Move from higher-timeframe objective to the setup area and execution timeframe.

concepts.title: Lower-timeframe confirmation
concepts.definition: An observable event qualifies a lower-timeframe entry under the selected model.
concepts.rule: Write the required break, close or retest before price reaches the area.
concepts.example: A required close through a swing completes before entry.
concepts.lookalike: A still-open candle is recorded as confirmed.
concepts.objective: State the exact close, break, or retest required by the chosen model.

concepts.title: Original consolidation
concepts.definition: An initial bounded range anchors the model narrative.
concepts.rule: Mark both sides before identifying the expansion.
concepts.example: Several bars establish a range followed by delivery away.
concepts.lookalike: A single arbitrary candle is used as an entire consolidation.
concepts.objective: Identify the initial range and mark its boundaries.

concepts.title: First-side delivery
concepts.definition: The initial leg carries price toward the first-side liquidity objective.
concepts.rule: Label the direction, reference and current phase.
concepts.example: Price delivers toward marked sell-side liquidity.
concepts.lookalike: A later bullish return is labeled the initial sell-side leg.
concepts.objective: Trace the initial movement and its objective.

concepts.title: Smart money reversal
concepts.definition: Evidence of a transition develops around the model’s reversal area.
concepts.rule: Separate the candidate turning point from subsequent confirmation.
concepts.example: A low run is followed by the required bullish shift.
concepts.lookalike: A low wick alone is treated as confirmed reversal.
concepts.objective: Mark the candidate transition and the evidence that would confirm or invalidate it.

concepts.title: Opposite-side delivery
concepts.definition: After reversal, price delivers toward objectives on the opposite side.
concepts.rule: Track subsequent targets in chronological order.
concepts.example: Bullish delivery reaches successive internal objectives after a reversal.
concepts.lookalike: A target preceding the reversal is counted as a later objective.
concepts.objective: Map the objectives after the reversal and track them in sequence.

sources.label: flux trades — How to Trade MMXM

concepts.title: First- and second-stage entries
concepts.definition: Later model phases can offer distinct entry opportunities.
concepts.rule: Name both the phase and its specific trigger.
concepts.example: A second-stage continuation has a separately recorded trigger.
concepts.lookalike: A phase label alone is recorded as a filled entry.
concepts.objective: Identify the model phase, then name the actual trigger used to enter.

sources.label: flux trades — Entries for Every Phase

concepts.title: Seek and Destroy
concepts.definition: A two-sided session can run liquidity in both directions.
concepts.rule: Monitor both boundaries and reassess directional evidence.
concepts.example: Both session extremes are run while directional setups fail.
concepts.lookalike: A clean one-direction expansion is labeled two-sided.
concepts.objective: Study a day that runs liquidity on both sides. Ask when the directional thesis became unreliable.

concepts.title: Next-day bias model
concepts.definition: TTrades uses completed daily price action to frame the next day’s conditional bias.
concepts.rule: Freeze the daily chart at the close and write the next session hypothesis.
concepts.example: Tomorrow’s objective is recorded before tomorrow’s candles.
concepts.lookalike: Tomorrow’s high is used to choose today’s anchor.
concepts.objective: Record tomorrow’s conditional plan using only information available at today’s close. Label this as TTrades’ interpretation.

concepts.title: Propulsion block
concepts.definition: A continuation area forms in the context of an earlier block and renewed delivery.
concepts.rule: Identify the earlier block interaction and subsequent continuation.
concepts.example: A supporting block interaction precedes another expansion.
concepts.lookalike: An isolated candle is labeled propulsion without context.
concepts.objective: Compare the continuation sequence with the order-block example in C21. Explain what qualifies the second structure.

concepts.title: Central Bank Dealers Range
concepts.definition: ICT’s forex range study derives reference levels from a defined dealing window.
concepts.rule: Reproduce the source window and record the price boundaries.
concepts.example: The marked range uses only bars inside the stated forex window.
concepts.lookalike: An arbitrary NQ morning range is called the original CBDR.
concepts.objective: Reproduce the original lesson’s range construction. Keep its forex context visible on the card.

sources.label: ICT Core Content — Central Bank Dealers Range

concepts.title: Standard-deviation projections
concepts.definition: Measured range multiples project reference prices from a specified anchor.
concepts.rule: Record anchor, range size and sign before projecting.
concepts.example: Lab arithmetic: a ten-point measured range projects twenty points at 2×. A midnight anchor is a custom lab variant requiring its own rule.
concepts.lookalike: The anchor is changed after the target trades, or a custom midnight rule is attributed to the original lesson.
concepts.objective: Document the anchor range and projection levels used in the lesson. Give any custom midnight anchoring rule its own **Lab adaptation** label.

sources.label: ICT — Institutional Market Structure & Standard Deviations

concepts.title: 8:30 a.m. New York opening price
concepts.definition: The opening price at 08:30 New York is a distinct intraday reference.
concepts.rule: Select the dated 08:30 local bar and record its opening price.
concepts.example: 08:30 opens at 20042 while midnight opened at 20010.
concepts.lookalike: The 09:30 cash open is substituted.
concepts.objective: Plot the 8:30 reference beside the midnight open and explain which reference the exercise uses.

sources.label: ICT — Episode 21, midnight and 8:30 opening prices

playbooks.title: ICT 2022 Mentorship setup
playbooks.summary: Study the sequence from a liquidity raid through displacement to a retracement into a fair value gap.
rules: Mark a prior extreme and a confirmed opposing swing before the raid.
After the raid, wait for displacement through that swing. Mark the resulting three-candle FVG and observe the first return.
Record the raid extreme as structural invalidation before entering.
Name an opposing liquidity objective that remains available.
Skip if the structure shift is missing or the objective has already traded.
Expire the idea at structural invalidation or the end of the planned session.
examples: Price sweeps a prior low, breaks a confirmed short-term high, then returns to a bullish FVG.
A gap appears after a sweep, but price has yet to break the reference swing.
Price reaches the objective before the first retracement.

playbooks.title: Silver Bullet
playbooks.summary: Look for a qualifying imbalance and a draw on liquidity during a specific New York time window.
rules: Choose 03:00–04:00, 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–15:00 America/New_York and mark a plausible liquidity objective.
Observe directional displacement and a qualifying FVG. Record whether its retracement occurs inside the selected window.
Mark the swing whose breach would defeat the entry premise.
Use a preselected liquidity objective beyond the entry.
Skip an unconfirmed direction, a filled objective or a window without a qualifying return.
Cancel an unfilled practice entry at the window close.
examples: A 10:18 displacement toward a prior high leaves a bullish FVG; price retests it at 10:24.
The retracement appears at 11:04 in the exercise using the 10:00 window.
The hour closes without an eligible imbalance.

playbooks.title: Judas Swing
playbooks.summary: Track an early session excursion beyond a range and the evidence for delivery in the opposite direction.
rules: Mark the earlier range, the chosen session and its opening reference.
Wait for the early excursion, a return inside the range and a confirmed displacement away.
Record the excursion extreme as the invalidation point.
Use the opposite range boundary or the next labeled liquidity level.
Skip if the range was selected after seeing the outcome.
Expire at a renewed move beyond the excursion extreme or session end.
examples: An early run above the premarked range reverses, breaks a swing low and retraces.
Price extends above the range and holds there.
The session remains entirely inside its earlier range.

playbooks.title: Turtle Soup-style failed breakout
playbooks.attribution: Lab adaptation of ICT chart examples
playbooks.summary: Test a failed breakout with an explicit close-back-inside rule.
rules: Choose the prior extreme and define the reclaim before viewing the next bar.
Observe a run beyond that level followed by a completed close back inside. Log an entry on the next eligible retest.
Invalidate beyond the failed breakout extreme.
Select an inside-range swing or the opposite boundary.
Skip sustained acceptance beyond the extreme.
Cancel the retest if price invalidates or the selected session ends.
examples: Price breaches yesterday's low, closes back above it and retests from above.
A wick approaches the prior low without trading through it.
Price reclaims but leaves without a retest.

playbooks.title: Optimal Trade Entry
playbooks.summary: Frame a retracement in the context of a previously selected impulse and directional objective.
rules: Select a completed impulse leg with a clear origin, terminus and objective.
Measure the leg and wait for the 62–79 percent retracement area. Require a completed lower-timeframe shift toward the objective in this exercise.
Invalidate if the impulse origin is breached.
Use the prior impulse extreme as the first reference objective.
Skip if the anchors change after the return or bias is undefined.
Expire after invalidation, objective touch or the session close.
examples: A bullish impulse retraces around 70 percent, holds its origin and produces the required shift.
The retracement breaches the bullish impulse origin.
Price expands directly without reaching the retracement area.

playbooks.title: Unicorn
playbooks.summary: Find the price intersection between a qualifying breaker and a fair value gap.
rules: Independently mark the breaker and the three-candle FVG.
Record their common price interval and wait for a first return with a close away in the planned direction.
Invalidate if price closes through the far boundary chosen before the return.
Select the next opposing liquidity level.
Skip if the two zones share no eligible price area.
Expire at invalidation or when the objective trades first.
examples: A bearish breaker overlaps a bearish FVG and price retests their shared interval.
A valid breaker is separated from the FVG by several ticks.
Both zones qualify but the retest occurs after the objective is reached.

playbooks.title: Inversion FVG entry
playbooks.summary: Study a failed FVG that price subsequently tests from the opposite side.
rules: Identify the original FVG and its boundaries before the breach.
Wait for a close beyond the far boundary and a retest from the opposite side with rejection.
Record invalidation across the retest swing.
Select the next liquidity pool in the new direction.
Skip a wick-only breach or a retest from the original side.
Expire if price reclaims the zone, hits the objective or ends the session.
examples: Price closes through a bullish FVG, returns from below and rejects it.
A wick enters the original FVG and the candle closes back above it.
The gap inverts, then price reaches the sell-side objective immediately.

playbooks.title: Market Maker Buy Model
playbooks.summary: Map first-side delivery toward sell-side liquidity, then assess the bullish reversal and subsequent delivery.
rules: Mark original consolidation, sell-side objective and a prospective bullish reversal area.
Following the sell-side run, require a bullish shift. Choose a specific retracement trigger before entry.
Invalidate at a breach of the selected reversal low.
Trace liquidity objectives back toward the original consolidation.
Skip if first-side delivery or reversal evidence is missing.
Expire at invalidation or completion of the mapped model.
examples: A sell-side run into a higher-timeframe area gives way to bullish displacement and a qualifying retracement.
A bounce inside the original range is labeled a completed buy model.
A reversal develops but the selected entry technique never triggers.

playbooks.title: Market Maker Sell Model
playbooks.summary: Map first-side delivery toward buy-side liquidity and the transition into bearish delivery.
rules: Identify consolidation, a buy-side objective and potential bearish reversal area.
After a buy-side run, require bearish displacement through a confirmed swing. Select an eligible retracement.
Invalidate at a breach of the selected reversal high.
Trace sell-side objectives toward the original consolidation.
Skip if price continues delivering higher without a bearish shift.
Expire at invalidation or completion of the mapped model.

Skip when the higher-timeframe thesis is unclear or the planned objective already traded.
